drhp.business: New Delhi Television Limited is a broadcasting and programming company whose entire turnover comes from broadcasting of news and related services. It runs English, Hindi, business and regional news channels together with a digital suite of news websites and apps, and has extended into international distribution across Connected TV, OTT/IPTV and digital platforms as well as a live-events vertical. Its customers include individual news consumers, television viewers, digital users, business and financial professionals, political stakeholders, advertisers and sponsors, and governments.

drhp.expansion: NDTV's expansion in FY 2025-26 is footprint- and platform-led rather than plant-led. Following the Adani Group's acquisition of a 64.71% majority stake in 2022, a transformation agenda was launched across operations, technology and content to strengthen distribution, modernise infrastructure and build a newsroom for the next era of media. Channel and platform build-out has proceeded in steps: NDTV Madhya Pradesh & Chhattisgarh, NDTV Rajasthan and NDTV World were launched in 2023 alongside a comprehensive brand refresh; NDTV Marathi was launched in 2024 together with expanded distribution …

litigation.note: The Board's Report (General Disclosures) records an Interlocutory Application filed by a Resolution Professional under Sections 43 and 66 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, challenging certain transactions undertaken by an erstwhile subsidiary, Indianroots Shopping Limited, in which the Company sold its majority stake in 2018. The Company has filed its response denying the allegations with supporting documents; the matter is pending before the NCLT and no adverse observation or order has been passed against the Company in any hearing so far. Other than this, no application has been made or is pending against the Company under the IBC. The report also states there were no significant or material orders passed by regulators, courts or tribunals impacting going-concern status, with penalties/adverse orders/show cause notices annexed as Annexure-E.

risks.note: Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk with negative financial implications. Data privacy risks encompass threats that can compromise the security and confidentiality of sensitive information, potentially leading to financial losses, reputational damage and legal repercussions, including data breaches, data discrimination and data brokerage. Cyber threats manifest as malware, phishing, ransomware and insider threats. Mitigations cited include a GlobalProtect firewall, Cisco Umbrella endpoint security, McAfee EDR with real-time threat detection, MFA-enabled VPN and Office 365 email, auto-patching, SAP for the finance system, regular security audits and employee training.

Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk with negative financial implications: any technology failure can disrupt the business, with primary threats around software architecture, tooling, delivery and maintenance. Mitigations cited include cloud-hosted email on Microsoft with standard SLAs, scheduled Veeam backups to LTO tapes with a HOT DR disaster-recovery setup for on-premise servers, entirely in-house broadcast operations (studio, PCR and transmission), and hosting of both the content management system and user-facing websites on Amazon AWS to mitigate site non-availability.

Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk with negative financial implications: regulatory compliance and good corporate governance form the foundation of the Company, and non-compliance in any form can severely impact the business, brand name and credibility. Mitigated by a team of professionals reviewing applicable laws and regulatory changes and monitoring timely compliance through a compliance management tool, backed by an online statutory compliance management system with periodic Audit Committee and Board review.

Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk with negative financial implications: failure to ensure employee health, safety and well-being can impact overall productivity and consequently business operations, customer satisfaction and profitability. Mitigations include regular reviews by Internal Auditors, an on-premises creche staffed with a doctor and trained attendants, supervised shuttle services at early and late hours for women, two doctors monitoring sick employees with a daily report reviewed by management, sanitisation, regular fire-safety exercises and hazard/near-miss reporting.

The Board's Report notes that in view of increased cyberattack scenarios, cyber security maturity is reviewed periodically and processes and technology controls are enhanced in line with threat scenarios, with real-time security monitoring across end-user machines, network, application and data layers. The Company states it did not face any incidents of data loss or data breaches in cyber security during the year under review - so the exposure is structural and managed rather than realised in FY26.
